from.place: The finite-tuple/cartesian-target construction in the classification proof: identify the product-diagram full subcategory of the relative exponential over N(Fin_*) with the canonical cartesian envelope.

title: Recognition of the cartesian envelope inside the relative exponential
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be an infinity category with finite products. Let $v:N(\Gamma^{\times})\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be the nerve of the cartesian fibration of pairs $(\langle n\rangle,S)$ with arrows over $\alpha$ whenever $\alpha^{-1}(T)\subseteq S$, and let $Q\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be the relative exponential of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] for $v$ and $\mathcal D$, whose $\langle n\rangle$-fiber is $\operatorname{Fun}(N(B_n),\mathcal D)$, where $B_n$ is the reverse-inclusion poset of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For each $n$, let $P_n$ be the full subcategory of diagrams $f:N(B_n)\to\mathcal D$ for which the restriction cone exhibits $f(S)$ as $\prod_{i\in S}f(\{i\})$, with $f(\varnothing)$ terminal. Let $P\subset Q$ be the full simplicial subcategory with fibers $P_n$. Then $P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ is canonically equivalent over the base to the cartesian symmetric monoidal infinity category $\mathcal D^{\times}\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Under this equivalence, the fiber over $\langle n\rangle$ is identified with $\mathcal D^n$, mapping spaces over $\alpha$ are the product of block mapping spaces, inert cocartesian arrows are exactly those with equivalences on the singleton components, and the equivalence preserves composition and all higher simplices; the space of such identifications with the specified product cones is contractible.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5(1)--(5), the product-diagram subcategory and its identification with the cartesian envelope.
